name: Hezekiah
title: Judah's Reformer King
summary: Hezekiah (Hiskia) was one of Judah's most godly kings, known for his religious reform, his trust in God during the Assyrian siege of Jerusalem, and his miraculous healing. He restored temple worship, removed idolatry, and relied on the Lord when facing the mighty Assyrian army under Sennacherib.

keyEvents.title: Religious Reform and Temple Cleansing
keyEvents.description: Hezekiah carried out a comprehensive religious reform. He opened and repaired the temple, removed the high places, broke down the idols, and destroyed the bronze serpent Nehushtan that Moses had made.

keyEvents.title: Celebration of Passover
keyEvents.description: Hezekiah invited all Israel and Judah to celebrate Passover in Jerusalem, the largest Passover celebration since the time of King Solomon.

keyEvents.title: The Assyrian Siege of Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: The Assyrian king Sennacherib invaded Judah and besieged Jerusalem. Hezekiah sought the Lord in prayer and received help from the prophet Isaiah, and God saved the city by sending an angel who struck down the Assyrian army.

keyEvents.title: Hezekiah's illness and miraculous healing
keyEvents.description: Hezekiah became mortally ill but prayed to God with tears. Through the prophet Isaiah, God promised him fifteen additional years of life, and as a sign, the shadow moved ten steps backward on Ahaz's sundial.

keyEvents.title: Visit from Babylonian envoys
keyEvents.description: Hezekiah showed the Babylonian envoys all his treasures. The prophet Isaiah warned him that everything would be carried off to Babylon, a prophecy about the coming exile.

keyEvents.title: The tunnel to the Pool of Siloam
keyEvents.description: Hezekiah built an underground water channel through the mountain to secure Jerusalem's water supply from the Gihon spring to the Pool of Siloam, a remarkable engineering feat.
